user_consequence: Clearing a yardage field (to retype it) instantly shows 0 in that field and the OUT/IN/TOTAL yardage footer recomputes from the coerced zero before the player finishes typing; if they tap away or the parent re-renders mid-edit, a transient wrong total is what's visible.
mechanism: FairwayHoleConfig.tsx:300 does value={hole.yardage} onChange={(e) => updateHole(hole.holeNumber, 'yardage', parseInt(e.target.value) || 0)} — there is no separate string edit-buffer; every keystroke writes parseInt(raw)||0 straight into committed hole state, so an empty/partial/NaN intermediate parses to 0 and immediately participates in frontYards/backYards/totalYards (lines 146-149) which the footer renders live.
expected: Section 9.2: Editing state preserves cursor/partial text with validation, not coercion — a cleared/partial field should not silently become a committed 0 that a derived total consumes.
actual: parseInt(...) || 0 commits a transient zero to state on every keystroke including clear/partial/paste/leading-zero/out-of-range/composition input.
proposed_fix: Keep a per-hole string edit-buffer (e.g. holes[i].yardageDraft: string) rendered in the input; parse/clamp only at an explicit boundary (blur, Save tap, or Enter), and only ever write a valid finite integer into the HoleConfig used for totals/validation. Reject/ignore paste of non-numeric text rather than coercing to 0. Cursor position is preserved automatically once the input stops being fully controlled by a numeric derived value.
accessibility_check: NOT_RUN — no VoiceOver/enlarged-text pass on this field this phase.

user_consequence: A hole seeded with par 6 (a legitimate validated value) shows no chip selected among the three visible options (3/4/5), looking like an error/unset state, and the player has no control that lets them choose or restore par 6 for a hole that should have one.
mechanism: handleSubmit's validity check (FairwayHoleConfig.tsx:157) allows par 3-6, matching comment line 8-9 ('par 3-6... kept VERBATIM'), but the rendered chip set at lines 267-293 hardcodes [3, 4, 5] only — there is no par-6 chip, so hole.par===6 never matches `selected` and no chip highlights.
expected: Every value the validator accepts should be reachable/representable in the picker (allowed par 6 vs. visible 3/4/5, per the work order).
actual: Par 6 is a silently orphaned valid value: seedable (from a baseline with a par-6 hole) but neither selectable nor visibly indicated once seeded.
proposed_fix: Either add a 4th/5th chip for par 6 (and par 3 6 range fully), or if product intends 3-5 only for manual entry, tighten the validator to match and handle a pre-existing par-6 baseline value explicitly (e.g. clamp with a visible one-time notice) rather than leaving the UI silently inconsistent with its own validation rule.

user_consequence: Tapping the already-selected par chip for a hole fires a haptic pulse for a no-op change, and re-clears any existing validation error even though nothing changed.
mechanism: The par chip onClick (FairwayHoleConfig.tsx:279-282) unconditionally calls fwHaptic('selection') and updateHole(...) without checking `selected` first, contradicting Section 9.4's rule that a repeated same value gets no feedback.
expected: Section 9.4: 'repeated same value... get none' (no haptic).
actual: Haptic fires regardless of whether the tapped par equals the hole's current par.
proposed_fix: Guard: if (selected) return; before firing fwHaptic/updateHole.

user_consequence: If the invalid hole is on the nine the player is not currently viewing, tapping 'Start round' shows a generic banner below the whole grid with no indication of which hole/nine is wrong, and the view does not switch to reveal it — the player must guess-and-hunt across 18 rows.
mechanism: handleSubmit (FairwayHoleConfig.tsx:156-167) computes one holes.every(...) boolean and, on failure, only setValidationError to one generic sentence (line 162) rendered once below the whole grid (lines 327-331) via a single InlineNotice. There is no per-hole/per-field error state and no logic to setActiveTab to the nine containing the first invalid hole.
expected: Work order: 'Place errors on the actual hole/field; reveal the correct nine before focusing an offscreen invalid field.' T13's invariant: 'correct field reveal'.
actual: One generic message, no nine-switch, no per-row indicator.
proposed_fix: Track which hole(s) fail validation; on submit failure, if the first invalid hole is on the non-active nine, setActiveTab to reveal it, and render an inline indicator on that hole's row (e.g. a red ring on the yardage input) in addition to (or instead of) the generic banner. Preserve all other holes' edits (already true — no regression there).

user_consequence: Documented for the record only — this is a verification that a previously real bug (9/18 toggle after course confirm not actually changing the seeded hole list) is fixed at this baseline, not a new defect.
mechanism: FairwayHoleConfig.tsx:120-138 compares a content-derived seedIdentity(initialHoles, holesPerRound) (not a reference) against the last-applied key on every render, re-seeding holes/activeTab/validationError whenever the baseline's actual content changes (course/tee/9-18/front-back), while leaving in-place edits untouched when the parent merely re-renders with equal content. Confirmed by commit d0a4a4724 'fix(golf): picking 9 holes after the course is confirmed still started 18 (#1732)' and the inline field-report comment (lines 124-130).
expected: G11: 'Baseline change resets local holes; define preservation and confirm replacements.'
actual: Already fixed — content-keyed reseed correctly distinguishes a real baseline change from a parent re-render. Open gap (see A05-006): no user-facing notice when a genuine baseline swap silently discards in-progress edits.
proposed_fix: N/A — verified fixed. See A05-006 for the remaining 'confirm replacements' half of G11.

user_consequence: A player who hand-tunes several holes (e.g., a long-tee yardage correction), then goes Back and changes Tee/9-18/Front-Back, returns to the Holes screen and finds every edit silently gone with no toast/banner explaining a replacement happened — only the persistent baseline banner naming the course, unchanged in wording, is visible.
mechanism: The reseed at FairwayHoleConfig.tsx:133-138 unconditionally overwrites `holes` with no side-channel notification when appliedSeedKey changes; baselineLabel (line 55, rendered 194-206) is static copy about the seed's source, not an event-driven 'your edits were reset' notice.
expected: Work order: 'Separate presentation changes from real baseline/course/tee changes... explain replacements.'
actual: A genuine baseline replacement is silent — no distinguishing UI moment tells the player their prior manual edits were just discarded.
proposed_fix: On a detected seedKey change where the previous `holes` differed from the previous baseline (i.e., the player had actually edited something), surface a brief one-time notice ('Your previous edits were reset because the tee/hole count changed') rather than silently swapping state. Product decision needed on exact wording/threshold — flagging as an open question, not prescribing UI copy.

user_consequence: No stored data distinguishes 'course hole 14' from 'round hole 5' for a Back-9 round, which is only a problem if some future/other consumer (Stats, cross-round hole comparison) assumes round hole-number equals course hole-number.
mechanism: Both FairwayNewRoundEntry.tsx's seedInitialHoles (~lines 170-187, explicit comment 'renumber 1..N regardless of front/back') and FairwayHoleConfig.tsx's seedHoles (line 81) deliberately renumber a Back-9 selection to holeNumber 1-9; grep across src/ found no courseHoleNumber/physicalHoleNumber/course_hole_number field anywhere, so no layer retains which literal course hole (10-18) was actually played.
expected: Work order: 'Retain actual course-hole numbering when playing Back 9; do not accidentally treat holes 10-18 as different physical holes merely because the UI renumbers a list.'
actual: This appears to be a deliberate, consistent product decision (round-relative numbering, like a standard 9-hole scorecard) rather than an accidental bug — both call sites document it identically. Whether any downstream consumer (A06 Stats/metric provenance, A10 schema) needs the literal course-hole identity for cross-round comparison is a product/architecture question this lane cannot resolve from round-setup code alone.
proposed_fix: Open question for the owner + A06/A10: does any metric ever compare 'this round's hole 5' across rounds that were played as different nines of the same course? If yes, a course_hole_number (or similar) needs to be added at the schema layer (A10) and threaded through here. If no, no action needed — mark this seed CANNOT_DETERMINE_WITHOUT_PRODUCT_DECISION rather than a bug.

user_consequence: A player who picks a cloud-tee course whose hole data is incomplete gets a round created with holes silently padded to par 4 / yardage 0, and is NEVER shown the Holes-config editor where they could notice or fix it — the round starts straight into shot tracking with invalid hole data baked in, no warning, no honest label.
mechanism: handleTeePick (new-round-client.tsx:1043-1081) pads missing cloud-tee holes with {holeNumber:n, par:4, yardage:0}. handleSetupSubmit's skip-to-tracking gate (lines 1326-1349) computes hasUsableConfig for a cloud pick as `h.par > 0` only (line 1334) — never checking yardage — so the padding (par:4) always satisfies it, FairwayHoleConfig never mounts, and persistRoundStart+setStep('tracking') (lines 1349,1380) fire immediately with the 0-yardage placeholder holes committed.
expected: Work order: 'Label imported, remembered and generic fallback pars/yardages honestly... Streamline known-valid setup while requiring missing essentials' — a synthesized/incomplete hole set should not silently bypass the one screen designed to catch it.
actual: An incomplete cloud tee produces a committed round with invalid (yardage 0) hole data and no player-visible review step, because the 'usable config' check only verifies par, which the fallback padding always provides.
proposed_fix: hasUsableConfig for a cloud pick should also require yardage > 0 (matching the manual-entry branch's own check), so an incomplete tee always routes through FairwayHoleConfig instead of silently skipping it. Independently, the padding at handleTeePick should mark padded holes so FairwayHoleConfig's baseline banner can honestly say 'some holes use estimated defaults' rather than implying every value came from the course.

user_consequence: A player watching the header's completed-hole counter after a save error sees the count as if the hole saved, while an error banner on the same screen simultaneously says it didn't — the two on-screen elements about the same hole contradict each other about whether it's durable.
mechanism: continue-round-client.tsx:880 sets completedHoleStats optimistically before persistCompletedHole's async checkpoint (lines 902-905) resolves; on a non-retryable hole_invalid failure (lines 812-814, returns false without touching completedHoleStats) or exhausted retries (lines 829-834), there is no rollback of the already-set completedHoleStats. The header badge (~lines 1519-1524, '{count}/{holes.length} saved') keeps counting the hole while the error banner (1531-1548) reports the same hole failed.
expected: Section 9.2: Sending/Definitive-failure must not read as Committed; the work order's 'truthful compact save status' goal.
actual: A failed hole checkpoint still increments the visible 'saved' counter, contradicting the simultaneous error banner.
proposed_fix: On a definitive hole-save failure, revert that hole's entry from completedHoleStats (or track a separate per-hole persisted-state map so the counter reflects only confirmed-committed holes), so the header count and the error banner never disagree about the same hole.

user_consequence: The 3-second success countdown and the 'Calculating your statistics…' submitting copy look like progress toward a finished analysis, but neither is connected to whether any real analysis job has started, is running, or has failed — a slow or broken analysis job is invisible on this screen.
mechanism: FairwayRoundSubmitOverlay.tsx: isSuccess = !!completedRoundId && !error (line 85) is the only 'commit' signal; the countdown (line 72, 122-132) is a fixed navigation timer; the submitting-state spinner (line 445, ring animation 420-433) is a pure CSS keyframe, not bound to any analysis-status prop or poll.
expected: Section 9.2/work order: 'the existing three-second countdown is not review progress'; 'Analysis preparing: a real post-commit job is pending... optional analysis retry does not resubmit.' Completion must separate committed-round from analysis-readiness.
actual: Countdown and spinner are decorative navigation timing, not a reflection of real analysis-job state; there is no visible analysis-readiness signal on this screen at all (deferred entirely to whatever the destination route does, which is outside this file — flagged to A06 for the review/analysis-status screen itself).
proposed_fix: Add an explicit analysisState prop (preparing/ready/failed) sourced from a real post-commit job signal; let the countdown/spinner reflect that state (or replace the fixed timer with a state-driven transition), and ensure the round-review destination lets a failed analysis retry without resubmitting the round (coordinate with A06 on where that retry lives).

user_consequence: On a submit error, the overlay tells the player 'Your round data is saved and won't be lost' unconditionally — even in a hypothetical case where the local persistence write itself also failed (e.g., a full-storage device), the same reassuring copy would still show.
mechanism: FairwayRoundSubmitOverlayProps carries no isPersisted/persistence-state field; the 'saved and won't be lost' text (lines 366-368) renders whenever `error` is truthy, with no gate on an actual confirmed-local-write signal.
expected: Work order: 'unconditional "won\'t be lost" language lacks an explicit persistence-state prop.'
actual: Confirmed — the claim is unconditional prose, not driven by any persistence-state prop.
proposed_fix: Thread an explicit isLocallyPersisted/persistenceState prop from the caller (which does know emergencySave's boolean result and/or offline-queue enqueue outcome) and only show the reassurance copy when that state is actually true; show a different, honest message on the rare case local persistence itself failed.

user_consequence: None currently reachable — this is a landmine for a future change, not a live defect.
mechanism: sync-engine.ts's manual-conflict-resolution API (handleConflict 865-922, detectConflict 1085-1151, resolveConflict 1156-1234, pendingConflicts, onConflictDetected, enableManualConflictResolution) has zero callers anywhere in the repo and is never enabled; the real, live conflict policy for rounds lives entirely in continue-round-client.tsx's roundConflictBlockedRef + server-side optimistic-lock check (verified by a sibling investigation this lane ran). If this dead API were ever wired up, its client_wins/merge strategies would violate T12 by silently overwriting server-authoritative data.
expected: Work order: 'Reuse the existing sync engine; do not implement a second queue hidden behind a new banner' — the inverse risk here is a reader mistaking dead code for the live conflict policy, or a future author wiring it up and reintroducing T12.
actual: Dead code, currently harmless, but documents a conflict-resolution strategy (client_wins/merge) that contradicts the live, tested policy elsewhere.
proposed_fix: Either delete the unused manual-conflict-resolution API or clearly mark it experimental/unused in a header comment so a future maintainer does not wire it up believing it is the sanctioned conflict policy.

user_consequence: None currently — no UI calls this path.
mechanism: offline-sync-store.ts's cancelSync (380-390) calls engine.stop(), which clears the auto-sync interval entirely rather than just aborting the current attempt; cancelSync has zero callers anywhere in the app.
expected: A 'cancel sync' affordance, if ever added, should cancel the in-flight attempt, not disable future background sync for the rest of the session.
actual: Dead code with a footgun: wiring a 'cancel' button to this function would silently stop all future auto-sync until the next full initialize().
proposed_fix: If a cancel-sync UI is ever added, distinguish 'abort this attempt' from 'stop the schedule' at the engine API level before wiring a button to it.

user_consequence: A rare double-tap or race during qualifier selection could momentarily show a stale available-rounds list right before the app redirects into an existing round.
mechanism: getNextQualifierRoundNumber fires on every selectedQualifierId change (new-round-client.tsx lines 897-943) and can redirect to an existing activeRoundId (line 915); the setup form remains fully interactive during that async window with no visible lock, so a fast double-tap on 'Start round' before the redirect lands is theoretically possible.
expected: No stale state visible/actionable during an async qualifier-round-number resolution.
actual: RISK only — source permits the window; not reproduced, needs a runtime.
proposed_fix: Consider disabling Start-round while the qualifier round-number lookup is in flight, or accept as a narrow/rare timing window given the existing duplicate-submit guard (A05 confirmed PASS elsewhere) likely catches any resulting double-create anyway.
